svg.aria-label: One Tensix core: five RISC-V dispatchers, L1, the compute engine and two NoCs
svg.title: One Tensix core: five RISC-V dispatchers, L1, the compute engine and two NoCs
svg.text: A Wormhole chip and one of its Tensix cores
one chip: 8 x 8 Tensix cores used by this op
link the two chips of an n300
two NoCs ring the mesh in
every core's L1 has a chip-wide
five "baby" RISC-V cores issue commands; the engines below do the work
compute kernel: one C++ source, compiled three times
L1 SRAM, 1.5 MB (about 1.41 MB usable by this op's buffers)
no cache: bytes get here only by NoC transfer or by the packer
compute engine (the three TRISCs drive it)
SFPU reads and writes DST in place
pack_tile: DST -> a CB in L1 (push_back)
Fig. A1. The reader and writer kernels move bytes between DRAM, other cores and L1 over the NoCs; the compute kernel moves tiles L1 -> Src -> FPU/SFPU -> DST -> L1.
